item.title: 12-year-old cellist from Massachusetts wins second place in national competition
item.description: Sofia Hernandez-Williams was the youngest semi-finalist in a prestigious classical music competition.

item.title: How the ICE crackdown in Minnesota has changed how people of color there move through the world
item.description: The flood of federal immigration agents in Minneapolis has people of color, even those who are U.S. citizens, living in fear.

item.title: Some blind fans to experience Super Bowl with tactile device that tracks ball
item.description: Some blind and low-vision fans will have unprecedented access to the Super Bowl thanks to a tactile device that tracks the ball, vibrates on key plays and provides real-time audio. About 10 blind and low-vision fans will have an opportunity to use the same technology at the Super Bowl when Seattle faces New England.

item.title: Major storm expected to miss Boston, with manageable snow falling on Cape Cod
item.description: The Boston-to-Providence corridor is looking at a few flakes, if any. But along the coast, the storm could still bring gusty wind and flooded roadways.

item.title: Massachusetts union members sue to block proposed income tax ballot question
item.description: A group of union members in Massachusetts and a director of a local nonprofit filed a lawsuit Thursday with the state’s highest court to block a potential ballot question to lower the income tax from appearing before voters in the November election.

item.title: A pattern of denial at the Department of Homeland Security
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said Minneapolis nurse Alex Pretti planned to “inflict maximum damage on individuals and to kill law enforcement.” But that’s not what eyewitnesses say and videos show. How can Americans trust an agency that disputes what we see with our own eyes?

item.title: Boston lawsuit aims to stop 'warrantless home invasions' by ICE
item.description: Lawyers say the Lyons memo undermines rights that legal advocacy groups try to help immigrants protect; they typically advise people to request a judicial warrant if ICE appears at their home.

item.title: Mass. reverses decision to send 8-year-old American in DCF custody to Guatemala
item.description: A state juvenile court halted a DCF plan to send U.S.-born child to Guatemala. Emergency court filings also raised new concerns about the father’s alleged criminal history.

item.title: Coast Guard finds body, debris field in search for missing Gloucester fishing crew
item.description: The Coast Guard launched a search and rescue mission early Friday after receiving an alert from the 72-foot Lily Jean about 25 miles off Cape Ann. They located a debris field near where the alert was sent along with a body in the water. It said it continued to be in search and rescue mode Friday evening.

item.title: As Arctic cold grips Boston, volunteers bring help to people sleeping outdoors
item.description: WBUR's Lynn Jolicoeur spoke with people who are unsheltered to ask how they're coping in the Arctic cold with the help of the volunteers.
